items.title: Two groups verify mathematician’s claim that Claude helped prove mathematics problem
items.summary: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge says it took him six weeks using Claude to crack the Riemann hypothesis, one of the most famous unsolved problems in mathematics. Two independent groups have since checked the claim and say it holds up, and a formal Lean proof-verification writeup of the result has also circulated.
items.why_it_matters: A verified AI-assisted proof of a 19th-century Millennium Prize-class problem would be one of the biggest demonstrations yet of AI as a genuine mathematical research partner.

items.title: OpenAI Chief Scientist Urges Industry Limits on AI Development
items.summary: OpenAI's chief scientist proposed that AI companies agree to limits on developing increasingly powerful models until researchers have better ways to understand and monitor their behavior. The proposal centers on how to even measure the "speed" of AI development before a speed limit can be set.
items.why_it_matters: A call for self-imposed industry limits from inside a frontier lab signals growing concern about the pace of capability gains outrunning safety understanding.

items.title: California Nvidia Probe Covers Potential Criminal Law Violations
items.summary: California's investigation into whether Nvidia illegally sold advanced chips to China and misled investors about that conduct is also examining potential criminal violations of state law, raising the stakes for the chipmaker. Separately, an associate referred to as Alice Huang has been accused of funneling Nvidia chips to China, and reporting has linked Alice Huang to firms with ties to China's military.
items.why_it_matters: A criminal dimension to the chip-smuggling probe raises the legal exposure for Nvidia well beyond a civil or regulatory matter.

items.title: What Nvidia’s Interim CEO, Colette Kress, Said to Employees After Jensen Huang’s Resignation
items.summary: At an all-hands meeting, Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress sought to put Jensen Huang's resignation behind the company. Coverage elsewhere describes a governance reckoning for Nvidia's board amid outside pressure to bring Huang back, concerns about his handshake-deal culture, and earnings results that contrast with the turmoil around his departure.
items.why_it_matters: Leadership instability at the company that supplies the chips underpinning most of the AI industry has knock-on implications for the whole sector.

items.title: International UN talks on controlling use of autonomous weapons collapse
items.summary: A week of UN talks aimed at establishing a negotiating mandate for a binding treaty on autonomous weapons collapsed just before 5am after all-night talks failed to overcome Russian objections, despite most states at the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons favoring progress. The Red Cross separately warned it will soon be too late to put the "genie back in the bottle" on these systems.
items.why_it_matters: Failure to agree even a mandate to negotiate leaves autonomous weapons development effectively unregulated at the international level.

items.title: Thinking Machines wows with Inkling 2 Mini looped transformer model that runs locally on laptops
items.summary: Thinking Machines Lab, the startup led by former OpenAI CTO Mira Murati, released Inkling 2 Mini, an open-weights multimodal looped-transformer model engineered to run offline on a 32GB MacBook Pro or a single desktop GPU, challenging the dominant cloud-based frontier model paradigm.
items.why_it_matters: A capable multimodal model that runs fully offline on consumer hardware pushes back against the assumption that frontier AI must live in the cloud.

items.title: Perplexity and Intelligence
items.summary: OpenAI published a piece on how perplexity is used to measure progress in AI models, arguing it could give developers a shared, common approach to evaluating emerging model capabilities.
items.why_it_matters: Shared, rigorous ways to measure model progress matter for the whole field, not just OpenAI, since current capability claims are hard to compare across labs.

items.title: Amazon closes in on $7.5bn deal to buy AI start-up Decart
items.summary: Amazon is closing in on a $7.5bn deal to acquire AI start-up Decart, a move that would help AWS compete with Nvidia in the race for computing power.
items.why_it_matters: A deal of this size shows how aggressively cloud providers are moving to secure AI compute capacity outside Nvidia's ecosystem.

items.title: Tech suppliers raise AI server prices up to 45% months after deals are signed
items.summary: Dell, HPE, Lenovo and Supermicro are demanding more money for AI server equipment months after deals were signed, with the increased costs hitting trading firms that rely on this hardware.
items.why_it_matters: Retroactive price hikes on AI server hardware signal tightening supply and rising costs across the AI infrastructure buildout.

items.title: Anthropic’s record IPO collides with tech’s worst week on Wall Street since 2020
items.summary: Anthropic's historic Nasdaq debut landed a day before Nvidia's stock closed out its longest weekly losing streak since 2008, as the broader tech sector sold off. Other coverage frames this as a disconnect between Wall Street's AI-spending worries and Silicon Valley's continued bets on the sector, with early backers describing what gave them conviction to invest.
items.why_it_matters: The market's rocky reception of the AI industry's biggest IPO to date is a read on investor confidence in the whole AI boom.
